questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Nice weather and a good time. Overall a gut feelling and advice from people who knew the city and area.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: This is my second exchange and even though they've been very different I cant recommend it enough. It is a lot of annoying practical things to do but it is such an enriching experience in total.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Somewhat easy. The university webpage is informative but not very user-friendly, however the physical office was very friendly and it didn't take long to realise that in Italy nothing is a hard deadline and at some point, sooner or later things will fall into place. But nothing is as strict and rigid as in Scandinavia. This is frustrating but liberating.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Assistance of what courses are actually available at what times. The app was also quite helpful for choosing course and planning your timetable.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I got a place recommended from a former exchange student through the housing page 'spotahome'. However I know other students who found housing through other pages. Those pages makes it feel safer with less risk of scamming, but they do take fees.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: To my experience there was no on campus housing. Milan has tons of nice areas so just make the best of your area and get to know the local spots.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Pretty easy the Erasmus-office is very helpful - but at least for Italy just lean back in the chaos, again things will get done at some point. Most thigs can be delayed, prolonged or just pushed to later on.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I received a mail with the address of the office and its opening hours, and when I arrived I went there and got my paper signed(the paper of attendance). Also I received a student card. Generally just read the e-mails thoroughly.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Very friendly and kind people at the office, answering whatever questions might occur.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Quite, most of the English taught courses were available. It was more a question of making the timetable that I wanted. I weren't declined any of the courses I applied for when I arrived. It was not the courses I got approved before hand, because some of them were autumn courses, courses no longer being active or not in English anyways. But ones I got the app it was easier to see what was actually available.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Follow the e-mail instructions and go with the flow. Do as they say in the office and things will eventually work out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I wasn't there for the teaching and in general there is a different less critical culture of academia. Interesting courses but not very giving or challenging compared to Copenhagen. There are still essays to be written and exams, but the exams focus more on what you remember from the courses rather than critical analysis.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took only courses on masters level because they were taught in English. They weren't very challenging but it can be a bit challenging to figure out what is expected of you in exams and essays.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: A lot more of remember these 'facts' and a lot less analytical and critical work. Really kind teachers, but mainly they are talking and lecturing.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1. "Global Intellectual History(9ects)" 
2. "Representations of Value, from clay tablets to cryptocurrencies(9ects)" 
3. "Intellectuals, Popular Culture, Collectives Identities: Italy and Europe in the 19th and 20th century(9ects)" 
4. "Iconology and Iconography(3ects)"

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend most of them, not all will continue though. Most courses depend a lot on the professor.

Food DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Not so much more or less expensive. I had saved a lot of money and therefore also spend a lot more money than I usually do. Eating at restaurants often, which is cheaper than in Copenhagen, but not as cheap as eating at home. Also i shopped a lot more than necessary. Some of the cost listed here might also overlap one another.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: I spend a lot more money abroad than what I normally do, just because I decided to spend money on fun things and things I could only do here. I do recommend saving some money before hand if possible, I gave me a lot of freedom to experience things. But you can also live way less expensively than what I did.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think there were some and usually they write about them in e-mails and then you can part take or not. I didn't really part take in any of them but et other students by coincidence.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you're on your own go to the events for erasmus students and talk to some people there.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I recommend going swimming, walking, visiting the city and areas around the city. Go to bar and restaurants and have fun.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easily, the Italians are quite open and curious, so just go with the flow and talk to strangers.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Talk to them if you find them interesting, invite them on a drink. If you are on your own its easier to get into talking to the local students, most of the students of my classes were non-Italians anyways.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not a lot, they eat late and almost all bars close at latest 2am. By then the metro doesn't run anymore, the trams are a bit flaky and the local ''monthly" rental bikes don't work at night. That means if you are out you'll have to pay for an uber or maybe a lime bike. I don't recommend walking at night, so it can get expensive in the long run.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The warm weather, the good food, the openminded people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Lean back in the practical chaos, it'll be fixed at some point.
2. Talk to some strangers and go out to the bars. 
3. Get the school stuff done fast rather than good, spend your time there doing other stuff, just get it over with and out of you way.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't care to much about school, even if you don't pass you'll get other tries. But usually you can pass somewhat easily. It can definitely be worth it to be 'non-attending' in some courses. If you attend you'll be exam on the lectures and maybe a book or two, if you don't attend you'll examed on maybe three books, which is easier because the professors just talk at lectures and it can be difficult to get good notes at the classes. When you are non-attending you have all of the material you'll get examed in.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The fun and good times, new friends and not having a job the days I were not in school. In that way it is less stressful than studying at home.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Just all the practical stuff beforehand and getting to know a new system.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
